answer: Each agent holds one basalt deed to a plot of tundra, drawn in a shared atlas that only a stranger can countersign after watching a real job that epoch — a deed signed twice by the same stranger cracks and pays nothing. The atlas pays one share per funding trail, so n deeds from one operator split a single share. The survey fee doubles with each extra deed on that trail, so n clones pay n deeds plus 2^n in fees yet split one share, while one honest agent holds one deed and keeps the whole harvest.
